# Directional Quantum Relay Limits

> Exact state-transfer limits for passive, static, local one-way quantum paths, with bounded-rate constructions and an optimized unavoidable-loss law.

## Scientific routes

- [Overview](README.md): physical question, central results, scope and reading routes.
- [Connected scientific account](science/README.md): ordered route through the model, proof, construction, loss frontier and consequences.
- [Model](science/model.md): passive Lindblad dynamics, arbitrary reference-entangled input, lower-bidiagonal complete drift, vacuum auxiliary modes, retained output, and rate conventions.
- [Path ceiling](science/path_ceiling.md): inherited weighted-shift product bound, positive convolution, sharp 4/e^2 ceiling and finite-time strictness.
- [Attainable designs](science/attainable_designs.md): local jump and Hamiltonian realization, slow endpoints, gamma-distributed transit delay, finite accuracy and time cost.
- [Loss frontier](science/loss_frontier.md): finite upper bound, exact reduction to maximal internal rates and endpoint/time optimization, matching exponential rate and weak-loss limit.
- [Channel consequences](science/channel_consequences.md): pure-loss capacity, finite-energy positivity, mode-count threshold, average qubit fidelity and assistance distinctions.
- [Bypass](science/bypass.md): exact static passive three-mode counterexample to an arbitrary-forward-graph ceiling.
- [Physical interpretation](science/physical_interpretation.md): local reservoirs, common-waveguide cascades, stored-state transfer versus traveling-field scattering, and resource accounting.
- [Finite examples](science/finite_examples.md): explicitly chosen finite designs, rigorous bounds, rate and waiting-time tables, and plotted asymptotic approach.
- [Related work](references/related_work.md): classical and quantum antecedents, verified source locations, inherited ingredients and reading limits.
- [Structured bibliography](references/references.bib): bibliographic records keyed consistently with the related-work account and the selected educational anchor.
- [Reproducibility](REPRODUCIBILITY.md): numerical commands, pinned packages, check scope and figure generation.

## Study route

The single educational anchor is Howard M. Wiseman and Gerard J. Milburn, Quantum Measurement and Control (2010).

- [Wiseman–Milburn bridge](learning/WISEMAN_MILBURN_BRIDGE.md): verified source sections, notation and damping conventions, a complete two-mode example, and the steps from open-system foundations to the path optimization.
- [30-milestone map](learning/MILESTONES.md): M01–M12 establish the background contract; M13–M30 build the scientific narrative from local ingredients to the global result and its limits. Each milestone states its understanding target, dependencies, conceptual connection and scientific sources.
- For the physical story, read the bridge, model and physical interpretation. For a theorem check, follow the scientific account directly. For numerical reproduction, use REPRODUCIBILITY.md and the canonical scripts rather than reconstructing formulas from the figures.

## Essential distinctions

- The physical drift has no upstream or bypass entries. A common chiral waveguide can generate additional downstream couplings and need not satisfy this condition.
- The 4/e^2 value is transmissivity or single-excitation arrival probability; it is not average unknown-qubit fidelity.
- Gamma caps engineered diagonal amplitude damping. Kappa is additional amplitude damping. Occupation decay rates are twice the corresponding amplitude rates.
- The classical numerical-radius product bound and Crabb profile, the two-emitter constant, and pure-loss capacity formulas are inherited.
- The finite positive-loss optimum is reduced to two endpoint rates and time. Equal endpoints are a construction, not a proved general finite optimizer.
- The weak-loss frontier and capacity range concern independently initialized channel uses. No fixed-spacing distance or per-second throughput is inferred.
